Subject: Renewal + expansion: proposed orchestration & cutover for reserved GPU pool

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the renewal conversation last week. Per our agreement in principle, this amendment ups your Dedicated reservation by +12 A100s (from 8 -> 20) and establishes a second reserved pool in us-east to support DR and peak throughput. Before we finalize terms, the Engineering/Operations teams want to confirm the rollout and cutover cadence so your production traffic experiences no more than 95th-50ms tail latency and we keep throughput at or above 3.2x your current baseline while we scale.

Below is a high-level plan to review; please confirm any blackout windows or additional SLAs you need:

- Proposed cutover window: Sat, 29 May 2026 02:00 - 06:00 UTC
- Canary phase: 0 -> 2 -> 10 -> 30 -> 100% traffic over 4 hours (pacing rules below)
- New pool: 20 GPUs (A100-sim), reserved in us-west2-primary and passive us-east1 for DR
- Throughput guarantee: baseline x3.2 with 99.5% availability during business hours (M-F 08:00-18:00 local)
- Fallback: automatic rollback to old pool if 5xx rate > 0.5% for 10 consecutive minutes
- Monitoring: token latency, queue depth, eviction rates, KV cache hit rate, and cost delta

Attachments: I attached the renewal amendment draft (renewal_amendment_v3.pdf) and a canary_playbook template for your ops team to review.

Next steps: if this looks good, we can lock dates and send the DocuSign amendment. If you want a different weekend or a weekday night, tell me and we’ll accommodate.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer

Team / Alice —

Attaching a concise checklist and run commands we will use during the canary. High level technical playbook (excerpt):

1) Pre-cutover (T-24h):
   - Validate pool health: run "rwctl pool status --pool acme-dedicated-2026"; all nodes must be Ready/Stable
   - KV cache warmup: replay top 500 hot prefixes to new pool in read-only mode
   - Load test: synthetic QPS at 1.5x baseline for 30m to validate thermal characteristics

2) Canary orchestration (operator-driven with automation):
   - Step 0 (1%): route 1% traffic to new pool via weighted LB rule; monitor for 30m
   - Step 1 (5%): increase to 5%; run perf-snapshot (latency, evictions, GPU mem usage)
   - Step 2 (20%): run KV miss analysis and compare RPS distribution
   - Step 3 (50%): enable prefix caching migration and check 95/99 latencies
   - Step 4 (100%): cutover and decommission old pool for customer-specific namespace

3) Rollback automation:
   - Run "rwctl rollback --from acme-dedicated-2026 --to acme-dedicated-2024 --reason <id>"
   - Notify on-call, open incident in Jira ACME-POOL-INC if rollback triggered

4) Post-cutover validations (T+1h, T+6h, T+24h):
   - Traffic parity: total tokens/sec within +/-10% of expected projection
   - Quality smoke tests: sample 100 responses for regressions (we will provide harness)

Escalation contacts:
   - Connor O'Brien (on-call infra): +1 (650) 555-0199
   - Rishi Malhotra (delivery): +1 (415) 555-0175
   - ACME Ops pager: ops@acmehealth.com

I validated that no DNS TTL changes are required — heatless traffic shift at LB is safe and reversible. I also attached canary_playbook.xlsx with command snippets and the throughput_projection_q3.csv we used for capacity planning.

Connor
